top_story_title: CISA adds an actively exploited Cisco Expressway flaw to KEV - the CVE is not named in the reporting
top_story_summary: CISA added four vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation. One of the four affects Cisco Expressway, Cisco's collaboration edge traversal appliance, which is normally published directly to the internet for mobile and remote access and business-to-business calling. The other three - Apache Roller, SAP NetWeaver and Broadcom VMware vCenter - are outside the scope of this digest, but they place the Expressway entry in a wave of edge and management-plane exploitation reported alongside a suspected China-nexus vCenter zero-day campaign.
top_actions: Open the CISA KEV catalog and the corresponding Cisco security advisory and record the exact Cisco Expressway CVE and affected release trains - this report does not state them, and CVE-2026-129448 is the Apache Roller entry, not the Expressway one.
Inventory every Expressway-C and Expressway-E node with its running version, and confirm which of them answer on a public address.
Confirm the running version against the vendor's fixed-release table and schedule the upgrade inside the change window; where nodes are clustered or paired, upgrade the secondary first.
Remove management access (HTTPS/SSH/API) from any internet-facing interface on the edge node; restrict administration to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.

Because exploitation is confirmed, treat affected nodes as suspect: after patching, rotate local admin credentials, API keys, device certificates and any stored service-account secrets - a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.
executive_summary: CISA added an actively exploited Cisco Expressway vulnerability to KEV. The reporting does not name the Expressway CVE - take the ID from the catalog and the Cisco advisory before scoping any change window.

A shared-component wave hit two major network vendors at once: OpenJDK CVE-2026-114938 and five nginx CVEs now have portfolio status pages open at both Cisco and Palo Alto Networks, both rated critical by Palo Alto.

nginx states fixed upstream releases (1.31.9 mainline, 1.30.7 stable) for its five CVEs; neither vendor's appliance-side fixed build is stated yet. Track the advisories rather than waiting on a patch that may not be published.

Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys can be brute-forced in seconds after a flawed 2025 key generation ceremony. Audit trust stores on firewalls, VPN gateways, TLS-inspecting proxies and management platforms for eMudhra roots.
Nothing in this window is genuinely AI-related; the AI section carries forward.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Retrieve the exact Expressway CVE from the CISA KEV catalog and the corresponding Cisco advisory before scoping work - do not infer it from this story.
**Cisco** — Build the target list from asset inventory filtered by model and running version: every Expressway-C and Expressway-E node, with a note on which have public addresses.
**Cisco** — Watch the Cisco advisory for the affected-product list and per-product fixed builds; do not plan a maintenance window against an appliance version that has not been published.
**Cisco** — Meanwhile, identify from asset inventory which Cisco appliances expose a web administrative interface or a published web or mail proxy service, and record their running versions.
**Cisco** — Track the Cisco advisory for the affected-product list and fixed releases; it is explicitly incomplete at publication.
**Cisco** — Identify from asset inventory which Cisco management, policy and controller platforms in the estate are Java-based, and record their running versions and patch levels.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Read the vendor status page for CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 and record the per-product verdict and any fixed PAN-OS, Panorama or Prisma Access build; re-check it rather than treating today's verdict as final.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Inventory firewalls, GlobalProtect portals and gateways, and Panorama instances with running versions, so the upgrade list is ready the moment fixed builds publish.

headlines.title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
headlines.summary: CISA added an actively exploited Cisco Expressway flaw to the KEV catalog alongside Apache Roller, SAP NetWeaver and vCenter bugs; the Expressway CVE is not named in the report.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco opened an advisory for five critical nginx remote code execution flaws affecting nginx 1.9.5 through 1.31.8, with Cisco's own affected-product list still to be published.

headlines.title: Vulnerability in Oracle OpenJDK (Java4Shell) Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco is tracking the impact of OpenJDK remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-114938, which affects Java 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 when processing Base64 content.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-123633 Portfolio Status: Impact of NGINX Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)
headlines.summary: Palo Alto Networks opened a critical-rated portfolio status page for nginx flaws CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, with product impact still being assessed.

headlines.title: CVE-2026-114938 Portfolio Status: Impact of Java Vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)
headlines.summary: Palo Alto Networks opened a critical-rated portfolio status page for OpenJDK flaw CVE-2026-114938, the same Java bug Cisco is tracking across its products.

headlines.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
headlines.summary: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CAs can be brute-forced in seconds after a flawed key generation ceremony, forcing an emergency trust-store distrust across products.
